title: UNIT 7: TEMPERATURE AND THERMOMETRY
notes:
✓ Temperature → Describes the degree of hotness or coldness of an object and is related to the average kinetic energy of its particles.

✓ Thermometry → Measurement of temperature using thermometers and temperature scales.

title: 7.1 TEMPERATURE AND OUR LIFE
notes:
✓ Temperature → Important physical quantity in everyday life and science.

◆ EFFECTS OF TEMPERATURE
✓ Weather and climate.
✓ Human health and body temperature.
✓ Cooking and food preservation.
✓ Industrial processes.
✓ Agriculture.
✓ Machines and technological systems.

✓ Temperature → Tells how hot or cold a body is and determines the direction of heat transfer.

title: 7.2 EXTREME TEMPERATURE SAFETY
notes:
✓ Extreme temperatures → Can be dangerous to humans, materials and equipment.

◆ HIGH TEMPERATURE
✓ High temperature → Can cause burns, dehydration, heat exhaustion and heat-related illness.

◆ LOW TEMPERATURE
✓ Low temperature → Can cause hypothermia, frostbite and damage to materials.

◆ SAFETY MEASURES
✓ Avoid direct exposure to extreme temperatures.
✓ Use appropriate protective clothing and equipment.
✓ Handle hot objects carefully.
✓ Keep away from unsafe heat sources.
✓ Take appropriate precautions in very cold environments.

title: 7.3 TEMPERATURE CHANGE AND ITS EFFECTS
notes:
✓ Temperature change → Can change the physical properties and state of matter.

◆ EFFECTS OF HEATING
✓ Expansion.
✓ Change of state.
✓ Changes in pressure or other physical properties.

◆ EFFECTS OF COOLING
✓ Contraction.
✓ Change of state.
✓ Changes in physical properties.

✓ Materials → Respond differently to temperature changes.

title: 7.4 MEASURING TEMPERATURE WITH DIFFERENT THERMOMETRIC SCALES
notes:
✓ Temperature scale → Assigns numerical values to temperatures using fixed reference points.

◆ CELSIUS SCALE (°C)
✓ Ice point → 0°C.
✓ Steam point → 100°C.

◆ FAHRENHEIT SCALE (°F)
✓ Ice point → 32°F.
✓ Steam point → 212°F.

◆ KELVIN SCALE (K)
✓ Ice point → 273.15 K.
✓ Steam point → 373.15 K.

✓ Kelvin → SI unit of thermodynamic temperature.

title: 7.4.1 FIXED POINTS OF TEMPERATURE SCALES
notes:
✓ Fixed points → Reference temperatures used to establish a temperature scale.

✓ Lower fixed point → Melting/freezing point of pure water at standard conditions.

✓ Upper fixed point → Boiling point of pure water at standard conditions.

✓ Temperature scale → Constructed by dividing the interval between fixed points into equal parts.

title: 7.5 TYPES OF THERMOMETERS AND THEIR USES
notes:
✓ Thermometer → Uses a thermometric property that changes with temperature.

✓ Thermometric property → Physical property that varies with temperature.

◆ COMMON THERMOMETERS
✓ Mercury thermometer.
✓ Alcohol thermometer.
✓ Thermocouple.
✓ Resistance thermometer.
✓ Radiation thermometer.

✓ Different thermometers → Are used because they have different temperature ranges, sensitivities and applications.

title: 7.5.1 MERCURY AND ALCOHOL THERMOMETERS
notes:
✓ Mercury thermometer → Uses expansion of mercury as the thermometric property.
✓ Range → Approximately −30°C to 300°C.

✓ Alcohol thermometer → Uses expansion of alcohol.
✓ Range → Approximately −115°C to 78.15°C.

✓ Alcohol → Is useful for measuring very low temperatures because it has a lower freezing point than mercury.

title: 7.5.2 THERMOCOUPLE AND RESISTANCE THERMOMETER
notes:
✓ Thermocouple → Uses the voltage produced by a temperature difference as its thermometric property.

✓ Thermocouple → Can measure very high and very low temperatures.
✓ Approximate range → −270°C to 2300°C.

✓ Resistance thermometer → Uses the change in electrical resistance of a material with temperature.

✓ Thermocouple and resistance thermometers → Are useful in scientific and industrial applications.

title: 7.5.3 RADIATION THERMOMETER
notes:
✓ Radiation thermometer → Determines temperature from thermal radiation emitted by an object.

◆ ADVANTAGES
✓ Can measure temperature without direct contact.
✓ Useful for very hot or moving objects.
✓ Useful where direct contact is difficult or dangerous.

◆ APPLICATIONS
✓ Industrial processes.
✓ Motors.
✓ Machines.
✓ Glass industries.
✓ Electrical industries.

title: 7.6 CONVERSION BETWEEN TEMPERATURE SCALES
notes:
◆ CELSIUS ↔ FAHRENHEIT

✓ Tᶜ = 5/9(Tᶠ − 32)

✓ Tᶠ = 9/5 Tᶜ + 32

◆ CELSIUS ↔ KELVIN

✓ Tᴋ = Tᶜ + 273.15

✓ Tᶜ = Tᴋ − 273.15

✓ Temperature difference → 1 K is equal in size to a temperature difference of 1°C.

title: 7.6.1 FAHRENHEIT ↔ KELVIN
notes:
◆ FAHRENHEIT TO KELVIN
✓ Tᴋ = 5/9(Tᶠ − 32) + 273.15

◆ KELVIN TO FAHRENHEIT
✓ Tᶠ = 9/5(Tᴋ − 273.15) + 32

✓ Final answer → Always keep the temperature unit.

title: 7.7 THERMAL EXPANSION OF MATERIALS
notes:
✓ Thermal expansion → Increase in size of a material when its temperature increases.

✓ Cooling → Generally causes contraction.

✓ Thermal expansion → Occurs in solids, liquids and gases.

◆ APPLICATIONS AND EFFECTS
✓ Expansion joints in bridges and roads.
✓ Gaps in railway tracks.
✓ Bimetallic strips.
✓ Thermometers and temperature-control devices.
✓ Expansion of liquids and gases in technological systems.

title: 7.7.1 LINEAR EXPANSION OF SOLIDS
notes:
✓ Linear expansion → Change in the length of a solid when its temperature changes.

ΔL ∝ L₀ΔT

✓ Therefore → ΔL = αL₀ΔT

✓ ΔL → Change in length.
✓ L₀ → Original length.
✓ ΔT → Temperature change.
✓ α → Coefficient of linear expansion.

✓ Final length → L = L₀ + ΔL.

title: 7.7.2 COEFFICIENT OF LINEAR EXPANSION
notes:
✓ Coefficient of linear expansion (α) → Fractional change in length per unit original length for a 1°C or 1 K temperature increase.

α = ΔL/(L₀ΔT)

✓ Unit → °C⁻¹ or K⁻¹.

✓ Different materials → Have different coefficients of expansion.

title: 7.7.3 BIMETALLIC STRIP
notes:
✓ Bimetallic strip → Consists of two different metals joined together that have different coefficients of thermal expansion.

✓ When heated → The strip bends because the two metals expand by different amounts.

✓ When cooled → It bends in the opposite direction.

◆ APPLICATIONS
✓ Thermostats.
✓ Thermal switches.
✓ Fire alarms.
✓ Temperature-control devices.

title: UNIT 7 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
◆ TEMPERATURE
✓ Temperature → Measure of hotness/coldness; related to particle motion.

◆ TEMPERATURE SCALES
✓ Celsius → 0°C to 100°C between water's fixed points.
✓ Fahrenheit → 32°F to 212°F.
✓ Kelvin → 273.15 K to 373.15 K.

◆ CONVERSIONS
✓ Tᶠ = 9/5 Tᶜ + 32.
✓ Tᶜ = 5/9(Tᶠ − 32).
✓ Tᴋ = Tᶜ + 273.15.
✓ Tᶜ = Tᴋ − 273.15.

◆ THERMOMETERS
✓ Mercury → −30°C to 300°C.
✓ Alcohol → −115°C to 78.15°C.
✓ Thermocouple → Approximately −270°C to 2300°C.
✓ Resistance → Electrical resistance changes with temperature.
✓ Radiation → Thermal radiation; non-contact measurement.

◆ THERMAL EXPANSION
✓ ΔL = αL₀ΔT.
✓ α = ΔL/(L₀ΔT).

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Heating → Generally causes expansion.
✓ Cooling → Generally causes contraction.
✓ Different materials → Expand by different amounts because their coefficients of expansion are different.
